text:
dana: Heads-up — we just saw a big tail latency spike for gpu-pool-eu-west-1 around 08:16 UTC and k8s job queue backed up. Seeing NVLink link flaps and repeated AER bus reset messages on a few nodes. :eyes:
dana: Node IDs: rack21-node08, rack21-node09. rack21-node08 is showing Xid 13 and lots of AER errors — likely flaky GPU/link.
ops-bot: Alert: 1998765432 - nvlink_link_down detected on rack21-node08:gpu3 (08:15:42 UTC). Error rate: 34/min. ECC corrected: 112 -> 890 in last 10m.
ken: Can you paste dmesg logs and nvidia-smi output from node08?
maria: Also index of which workloads got rescheduled? Need to estimate capacity impact before we drain.
dana: Logs (tail):
```
[Aug 12 08:15:41] pcieport 0000:3d:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
[Aug 12 08:15:41] NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00:03: Xid (PCIe Bus Error) 13
[Aug 12 08:15:41] nvlink0: link 1 down, tlm err
[Aug 12 08:15:42] nvidia: GPU 3: ECC corrected errors increased
```
dana: nvidia-smi -q snippet:
```
GPU 3
    FB Memory Usage
        Total                       : 24576 MiB
        Used                        : 0 MiB
    ECC Errors (Volatile):
        Single-bit ECC errors: 112 -> 894
        Double-bit ECC errors: 0
    NVLink Error Count: 38
```
ryan: Sounds like intermittent NVLink physical layer issues. Might be cabling/riser or card seating. rack21 has had a few temp variations after the last maintenance window.
ken: For short-term mitigation we should cordon/evict GPU workloads off node08 and node09, failover to reserved capacity in eu-west-1-dedicated. Any objections?
maria: We have ~3.2k tokens/s demand from PLG traffic on that pool. Moving to dedicated will uptick cost but keeps latency SLOs. Recommend draining node08 first.
dana: Proposed steps: 1) cordon rack21-node08; 2) kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data rack21-node08; 3) move high-priority routes to dedicated pool via routing policy; 4) collect diagnostics and hardware introspect (pciutils lspci -vv, riser sensor).
ken: Add --pod-selector=app!=prometheus to avoid kicking monitoring unintentionally. Also snapshot metrics and traces before/after.
ops-bot: Runbook reminder: If node shows repeated nvlink down + Xid 13 and ECC grows >500 in 1h -> open RMA with vendor and schedule replacement.
ryan: I can do the physical check if needed. If reseating doesn't help, we'll RMA the GPU and swap in spare from spares rack.
dana: Quick check of scheduling impact: current pending pods: 12; evicting node08 should push 8 onto other nodes and 4 into pending until we scale dedicated.
maria: We should also temporarily lower batch sizes on gen endpoints routed to that pool to reduce burst allocation pressure. That saves tokens and keeps latency stable.
ken: Running cordon+drain in 2 mins. Copying commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon rack21-node08
kubectl drain rack21-node08 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=prometheus' --timeout=10m
```
dana: I'll run diag script concurrently: /usr/local/bin/gpu-diagnostics.sh --node rack21-node08 --collect dmesg,nvlink,pcie,aer,smartctl
ops-bot: diag job started (job id: diag-1998765432-1). Attach logs when done.
ryan: If drain doesn't finish in 10m, we should force-evict lower-priority jobs and fallback to reserved capacity.
maria: After we stabilize, let's re-evaluate autoscaler thresholds — we were at 65% headroom which isn't enough for 3k tokens/s spikes.
ken: Drain complete. Pod evictions: 8 succeeded, 1 failed (stateful job with local disk), 3 pending. Moving priority route to dedicated now.
dana: Diag outputs: nvlink electrical errors persist after soft-reboot. Reseated GPU, re-ran tests -> errors decreased but still present. Suggest RMA.
ryan: I'll tag hardware for RMA and schedule replacement during low-traffic window (12:00 UTC).
maria: For cost tracking, log the dedicated capacity bump under ticket INF-6642 so finance can attribute overage.
ken: Note: region eu-west-1 has limited spares — we may temporarily route a small percentage to eu-central if eu-west designated endpoints allow it. Any compliance objections?
maria: EU routing policy allows eu-central for non-sensitive requests. Ok to shift 10% as a safety valve.
dana: Postmortem checklist item: add NVLink link-flap alert that correlates AER/Xid with ECC growth and automatically suggests drain. Ticketed as INF-6643.
ops-bot: Incident summary logged to incidents channel with id INC-1998765432.
ryan: I'll bring the spare and swap tomorrow. For now, monitoring shows latency back within SLO after routing changes. :thumbsup:
